Subject: ACME: Model routing & policy architecture - Post-call recap

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: document summarization + smart Q&A across user support docs (low latency targets for interactive UI).
- Traffic profile: bursty web traffic, 200–400 QPS peak anticipated in early pilot, mostly US-based with some EU users.
- Security: Acme prefers OIDC SSO for service accounts; procurement will request SOC2 + custom DPA.
- Integration goals: embed Redwood SDK for server-side routing, use embeddings + reranker for recall layer, structured output for tool-calls (ticket creation integration).

Key technical topics to address (we'll cover in the follow-up tech deep-dive):
1) SDK setup & auth: server-side SDK, OIDC flow for short-lived tokens, KMS for model keys.
2) Model routing & policies: latency vs cost tiers, fallback chains (LLM variants), regional routing (us-west primary, eu fallback).
3) Embeddings & reranker: indexing frequency, vector size, and how reranking integrates before generation.
4) Structured outputs/tool calling: schema enforcement for ticket creation and external API calls.

Attachments: MVP-integration-checklist.xlsx (initial checklist), redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (SDK + auth notes).

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive (60m): Thu Mar 26 at 10:00 AM PT — confirm?
- We'll send a short architecture draft and a model-routing policy proposal ahead of the call.
- Procurement: please share point-person for SOC2/DPA requests (we can loop legal).

Please reply with confirmations and any additional integration constraints (VPC, private endpoints, SIEM exports).

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: ACME: Model routing & policy architecture - Post-call recap

Looping in the engineering notes for the deep-dive. Below is a concise proposal we can present — focused on the items Sara asked about.

1) Per-tenant routing policies
- Yes, Redwood supports per-customer policy profiles. Proposal: define 3 policy tiers for ACME pilot:
  * premium (latency SLO: p95 < 150ms, route to dedicated low-latency pool in us-west)
  * standard (balance cost+latency, route to mixed shared/dedicated)
  * cost-optimized (lower-cost quantized variants with higher latency tolerance)
- Policies include token budget caps, max concurrency, and autoscale thresholds.

2) Fallback chains / model variants
- Implement chain: primary -> fallback1 (smaller but same architecture) -> fallback2 (quantized or distilled family) -> cached-prefix response.
- For structured output/tool-calls: define a hard fail if parser confidence < threshold — trigger a deterministic fallback to rule-based extractor or enqueue for human review.

3) Embeddings & reranker control
- We expose embedding ingestion APIs and a scheduled refresh job. We can accept webhooks to trigger reindexing on document updates.
- Reranker sits between retrieval and generation: retrieval -> dense embeddings -> top-K -> reranker scoring with cross-encoder (if enabled) -> final prompt generation.

4) Auth & SDK setup
- Server-side SDK + OIDC: recommend short-lived signed JWTs via your IdP, SDK handles token refresh.
- For Private deployment (if needed) we support VPC endpoints and HSM/KMS integrations.

5) Regional routing
- Routing table example: user region -> preferred region; if capacity constrained or policy requires, route to secondary region with model variant compatibility.

6) Observability / SLAs
- We'll surface token-level latency, per-model p95/p99, and policy-level throttling metrics in the console. We can expose traces for failing structured outputs.

Attachments referenced in our slide deck during call: redwood-architecture-draft.pdf (will attach to the follow-up). Also add link to internal design doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-integration

Notes: we'll keep fallback policy conservative for the first 30 days to avoid regressions in structured outputs.

-dev
